doc.name: MorphaReels
doc.instructions: Morpha is a video editor for short-form social video, driven through these tools. Every tool call needs a signed-in connection: the person signs in through their MCP client (Claude Code: the /mcp menu) or the client sends a Morpha key as `Authorization: Bearer`; otherwise calls are refused. When the video is done, give the person the editorUrl from create_project, open_project or list_projects: they can adjust anything by hand and choose Share, then Download (Render MP4 on a phone): free, no watermark, in the browser. If those results carry a claimUrl the account is anonymous: give the claimUrl instead, so the project becomes theirs. Before changing a project call describe_video, then inspect_layers; end each change-set with save_version. Call show_project once per project: where the client renders views, it plays in the chat and follows each edit. Its result carries a placard per page, in page order: a Morpha card shaped like that page. TikTok and Instagram Reels draw their own buttons, captions and tab bar over the edges of a full-screen 9:16 video, and Instagram's feed crops tall videos to 4:5. describe_video's platform_safe_area is the part that stays visible (null when nothing is covered or cropped). Keep text, captions, logos, buttons and other key content inside it; backgrounds, footage and decoration can run to the edge. Text results and describe_video carry fits per text layer; if a warning says the text runs past the canvas or safe area, add \n line breaks or lower text_size to the size named. Versions or options of one video (styles to pick from, hooks, languages, a sheet's rows) are pages of ONE project (add_page, duplicate_index), never separate projects: the preview turns pages and exports one video per page. Refer to projects by name, never by id. MP4 export happens in the MorphaReels editor (Share, then Download); with a subscription, render_video renders on MorphaReels' servers and render_status returns the link. upload_image / upload_audio take a web URL.

tools.name: create_project
tools.title: Create project
tools.description: Create a new project and return its server-minted id. The id is an opaque v4 UUID assigned automatically, not chosen by the caller; people see the project's `name`. If the clone source lives in a workspace you can only view, the call FAILS rather than silently making a personal copy — pass workspaceId:null for a personal copy. The user's editor session won't auto-refresh — they'll need to reload to see the new project in the picker. Options or versions of one video (styles to pick from, hooks, languages) are pages of ONE project (add_page, duplicate_index), not new projects: the chat preview turns pages, and separate projects cannot be flicked between.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.title: Restore version
tools.description: Load a saved version over the live project. Accepts either the version's UUID `id` or the `v<N>` shorthand (e.g. `"v6"` finds the bookmark with version_number=6); auto-snapshots are addressable by UUID only. Without `page_index` this replaces the ENTIRE project (every page) — an auto checkpoint named `before restore: …` is saved first whenever the current state has unsaved changes, so the overwritten state stays recoverable. With `page_index` it restores ONLY that page: the page is matched across versions by its stable id and replaced verbatim (canvas size and name included); other pages are untouched and the write is compare-and-swapped against concurrent edits. Errors if the version predates that page — restore the whole version instead. A restored page may reference assets deleted since the snapshot; those render as missing. An open editor reconciles the result into the live project within a few seconds — no refresh needed.

tools.name: upload_image
tools.title: Upload image
tools.description: Upload an image into a project from a public http(s) URL or a file attached in the chat, fetched server-side. Pass `url` for a public http(s) link, or `file` for a file the person attached in the chat (an MCP client that supports file inputs fills `file` with a temporary download link itself; do not ask the person for a URL to something they have attached). The target is the URL you pass and nothing else: Morpha's Worker fetches it with a plain HTTP GET, following redirects, and identifies itself as "Morpha/1.0 (+https://morphareels.ai; hello@morphareels.ai)". No third-party API is involved. The URL and every redirect must reach a public address: private, loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are refused. The worker downloads the .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.svg, stores it in the project's asset bucket under a new id, and returns { filename, name, sizeBytes, contentType, width, height }: pass the returned `filename` (the file's id, never shown to a person) to add_image_layer, and `name` is what people see; `width` and `height` are the picture's own pixel size (null when its header did not say), so size the layer from them or pass add_image_layer one side and let it keep the aspect. This tool does not search for images: pass a direct image file URL, such as one the person has given you, and respect the licence its source states. A url must be a direct, publicly-fetchable http(s) link (not an auth-walled page). SVGs are rejected if they carry a <script>, an inline event handler, a <foreignObject>, a javascript: URL, or an external resource reference — supply a static, self-contained SVG. Buffered in Worker memory, so capped at 16 MB. A file on the person's own disk is uploaded in the editor. Reference: https://morphareels.ai/docs/tools#uploadimageurl-file-name

tools.name: set_layer_transition
tools.title: Set layer transition
tools.description: Set how a layer ENTERS at the start of its on-timeline window and LEAVES at the end, instead of popping. The transition is EDGE-RELATIVE — only a length and a look are stored — so it rides the edge through every later trim, slide or clip retime. Prefer this over fade_layer / apply_preset whenever the intent is 'enters and leaves nicely': those write opacity keyframes at ABSOLUTE frames, which strand themselves the moment the edge moves, and clutter the timeline lanes. A layer created WITH a `block` is born carrying a short fade at each edge — whether you passed the block or the editor minted one — so check `inspect_layers` before adding one, rather than assuming there is none. Layers created before this default existed, and any edge cleared to "cut", carry nothing and do need setting. A layer with NO block is always-present, has no edges, and a transition on it is inert. Video clips default to a hard cut, because a hard cut between shots is the grammar of short-form video. kind "cut" clears the edge back to a hard cut. The length is a request: when the window is too short to hold both ramps they are squeezed proportionally at render time, and the stored values are left intact.

tools.name: shift_group
tools.title: Shift group
tools.description: MOVE a group and everything inside it along the timeline, keeping its internal timing intact — the 'slide this whole section later' operation. tools.name: set_canvas_size
tools.title: Set canvas size
tools.description: Resize the ACTIVE page's canvas to width × height pixels. The composition is scaled UNIFORMLY to fit the new frame (a single factor s = min(newW/oldW, newH/oldH), so nothing distorts — a circle stays a circle) and then re-centred so the old composition centre maps to the new canvas centre. Every layer's position, size, group pivots, and x/y/width/height keyframes follow this fit+recentre; same-aspect resizes scale exactly, aspect changes letterbox the content centred. Each page owns its size, so this leaves sibling pages untouched — select_page then set_canvas_size again to resize another one. Common sizes: 1080×1920 (9:16 Reels/TikTok/Shorts), 1080×1350 (4:5 Instagram), 1080×1080 (1:1 square), 1920×1080 (16:9 YouTube).

tools.name: set_matte_source
tools.title: Set matte source
tools.description: Set (or clear) a track matte — the host shows only where the matte source is opaque. The HOST can be a leaf (image.<id>, video.<id>, shapes.<id>, text.<id>) OR a group.<id> (a group is a layer of sorts): a group host clips ALL its composited children to the source shape's path — e.g. a marching chevron strip + black backing shown only inside an arrow / band shape. For a leaf host the source can be any leaf (use a text.<id> source for video-/image-filled letterforms); for a group host the source must be a shape (shapes.<id>). The source is CONSUMED: it stops painting as a layer of its own, so do NOT set its opacity to 0 (an invisible stencil empties the mask and the host vanishes); hiding it changes nothing, since its hidden flag does not feed the mask. It has no time window of its own: it follows the host's, and attaching drops its block and edge transitions (`source_window_dropped` in the result). Its position, scale, rotation and keyframes shape the mask. Pass null to clear.

matte_inverted.description: Optional. Invert the mask (knock-out): the host shows everywhere EXCEPT where the source is opaque — a punch-through / spotlight. Honored on leaf hosts; ignored on group hosts. Omitted = preserve current; clearing the mask resets it.
